concept.reason: Real horned skull photograph, scaled museum skull and museum-commissioned whole-animal reconstruction available; no additional conceptual image needed.

scope: Original653 complete living horned adult, with bifurcating rostral horn and paired postorbital horns. Do not reduce to skull.
reference_specimens: FAM33407 horned skull, AMNH display photographed by Jonathan Chen2024
UF16154 skull without horn armament, Florida Museum official photo with10cm bar; used only for approximate cranial length, not horn shape
UCMP31520 type identified in Patton1969 original study

scale.cranial_length_status: Approximate photo-derived UF16154 dimension: skull approx880px versus10cmbar256px =>34cm. Not a direct specimen measurement and not the horned FAM33407 measurement.
scale.body_size_status: Artistic proportion estimates for a deer-like whole organism; not measured skeleton dimensions.
scale.horn_dimension_status: Artistic relative proportion from horned skull photograph; perspective prevents precise measurement.

material_policy: Restrained brown/taupe coat, lighter underside and dark muted horns/hooves. Coat colors are speculative; do not copy museum painting pixels, exact pattern or composition.
diagnostic_targets: One long midline rostral horn shaft from anterior snout, splitting only near distal end into two branches in transverse plane. Preserve readable Y fork and long single base; not two separate nose horns or forehead antlers.
A separate left/right postorbital horn pair arises behind eyes, sweeping outward then upward/inward. Smooth unbranched pair, not many-tined deer antlers.
Rostral fork and rear horn pair remain visually separated in front and perspective views, with open negative spaces.
Elongated ungulate muzzle, lateral eyes, ears distinct from horn bases; moderate neck, compact deer-like trunk, four slender limbs and short tail.
Four two-toed hoof contacts and clear fore/hind joints. Whole living animal, no detached skull or museum pedestal.
Horn geometry takes priority over fur or decorative details. Show original diagnostic combination at thumbnail size.
uncertainties: Body posture, coat, sex assignment of the restored living individual and soft tissues are reconstruction choices. Horn-bearing adult form chosen to preserve original scope.
UF16154 is not the horned skull. Do not claim its missing horns prove damage or sex; it only calibrates approximate cranial size.
Museum painting is a curated artistic reconstruction, not direct evidence of coat colors or exact body dimensions.
Horn surface coverage and details not scientifically resolved here; restrained smooth material without decorative rings.
acceptance_checklist: Whole organism with one bifid anterior nasal shaft plus separate paired posterior horns.
Front and perspective show fork opening and distinct rear horns; side shows rostral origin at snout, not forehead.
No excess antler tines, no duplicated nasal roots, no horn/ear floating pieces.
Anatomically connected quadruped with four split hooves and readable head/neck transitions.
Default4 exactGLB views, self-contained dependencies and two rebuilds; independent review separate.
